$comment: SOURCE, NOT GENERATED. How a release reads on the changelog, shaped after Preline's (Zafar, 17 Sep 2026, pointing at preline.co/docs/changelog.html): a title, then chips (an icon and a label, like Preline's "New Components & Improvements" and "Fixes and Improvements"), each followed by its items with a bold lead ("People:", "Layout:") and the drawings the item is about. His asks on the way: "topic > icons, topic > icons. not all topics first and then all icons after that", "categorize them, not just text > icons. titles, etc.", "redrawns deserve to be a separate topic, not within a topic and each subtitle must carry shareable link like the main titles". So redraws are always their own chip. Per version: `title` (the release's headline, which every version has, released ones included, because the page heads each entry by it) and optionally `sections`: chips with `title`, `icon` (a drawing from this set, by name), `text`, and items in `sections` with `title`, `text`, `names` (added) or `redraws`. A version with no `sections` is drawn with default chips, New drawings and Redrawn, straight off git. pipeline/build-history.mjs gives every chip and item an `anchor` (v<version>-<chip>, v<version>-<chip>-<item>) that the site links, keeps only the drawings the entry carries, and appends anything no item claims in a last untitled group, reported, so a stale list never drops a drawing. Keyed by the version the work ships as, so nothing is re-keyed at the tag. Numbers go in as {names} and {files}. Where a version has sections they replace the note.

1.0.0.title: Four styles, a People shelf and the panels on every side

sections.title: Four styles
sections.text: Every name now comes in stroke, two-tone, duotone and fill: {files} SVGs across {names} names. The outlined duotone is called two-tone from this release, so an import of duotone that wants the old look changes to two-tone. Duotone is a new style with no outline, a grey body with the part that matters in black, drawn icon by icon.

sections.title: People
sections.text: A new shelf for the boy, the girl, a baby with a curl, one with a bow, and both babies again with a pacifier.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text: The panels gain their close, open and dashed forms on every side, three split layouts and a table.

sections.title: Devices
sections.text: The phone takes call, incoming, outgoing, missed and forwarded. The tablet takes its upright form and the phone's eight signs, a laptop arrives, and the tablet and the laptop each sit beside a phone.

sections.title: Finance
sections.text: Two banknotes carry a check, minus, plus and x.

sections.title: Time
sections.text: The alarm clock takes a check, plus and minus, beside a stopwatch and its reset.

sections.title: Transport
sections.text: A rocket climbs on its flame, trails speed lines and stands upright.

sections.title: Pointers
sections.text: A closed hand and an open hand join the pointer.

sections.title: Arrows
sections.text: The big arrows point four ways.

sections.title: Text
sections.text: The heading comes with its six levels.

sections.title: Weather
sections.text: A snowflake and wind.

sections.text: A zipped folder.

sections.title: Redrawn
sections.text: Drawings that already shipped and were drawn again, each shown before and after.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text: The four dashed close panels sit their grey under the frame's round corners, and the grid fills keep 2 units clear of their edges.

sections.title: Devices
sections.text: In two-tone scan-eye greys its frame, and scan-search's handle starts on its ring.

sections.title: Finance
